Java Lesson 1 - Hello World
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Hello World lesson on Codecademy. The goal of this lesson is to learn how to create workspaces in VSCode, run java projects, and submit assignments on Classroom50. Connor will walk you through cloning the repository that is created when you accept this assignment.

Your task:
Print "Hello <your name>" to the console.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 2 -- Variables
assignments.description:
Your Task:
Save the following information in Variables. Think about what data type each variable should use, and use understandable names for each one (ex. Don't name your age variable "Bob"; name it "age"). Then, print out each of your variables.
- Your name
- Your age
- Whether you're right or left handed (Don't use a String)
- Hours of sleep last night (use decimals if applicable)

assignments.name: Java Lesson 3 - Manipulating Variables
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Manipulating Variables lesson on Codecademy. In this assignment, you will use variables and mathematical operators to make calculations. The goal is to practice changing variables and using Java to solve simple mathematical problems.

Template: Main class with the main method

Your task:
Create a program that calculates the cost of buying several items. Choose three items and save the price of each item in a variable. Then calculate and print:
- The total cost before tax
- The amount of sales tax
- The final cost after tax
- The average price of the three items
Use variables and mathematical operators to do all of the calculations. Do not calculate the answers yourself and just print the final numbers.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 4 - Classes
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Introduction to Classes lesson on Codecademy. This assignment introduces one of the most important ideas in Java: creating your own classes and objects. You will create a class that represents something and then create objects from that class. You can create a new class by creating a .java file in the same package (folder) as your main file.

Template: Main class with the main method

Your task:
Create a class that represents something of your choice. Some examples include a Robot, Dog, VideoGame, Car, or Student.
Your class must:
- Have at least 3 instance variables that describe the object
- Have a constructor that sets all 3 variables
- Use appropriate data types for your variables
- Create at least 2 different objects in main
- Give the objects different values
- Print information about both objects

Your class should represent something that makes sense to you. The goal is not to make the most complicated class possible, but to demonstrate that you understand how classes and objects work.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 5 - Methods
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Methods lesson on Codecademy. Methods allow you to break a program into smaller, reusable pieces. In this assignment, you will practice deciding when a task should be its own method and passing information into methods.

Template: Copy-paste your code from lesson 4; we are building off of that.

Your task:
Add at least 3 methods to your class. Each method should perform a useful action related to the object your class represents.
Your methods must include:
- At least one method that takes a parameter
- At least one method that returns a value
- At least one method that returns void
- Calls to all 3 methods from main

Your methods should actually use the information stored in your object. Avoid making methods whose only purpose is to print a single hard-coded sentence.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 6+7 - Conditionals & Control Operators
assignments.description:
Complete after doing both the Conditionals and Control Flow and Conditional Operators lessons on Codecademy. This assignment combines both lessons because the concepts are most useful when used together. Your goal is to make a program that can make decisions based on information.

Template: Main class with the main method.

Your task:
Create a program that determines what a robot should do based on several conditions. Choose your own scenario.
Your program must:
- Use at least one if statement
- Use at least one else or else if
- Use &&
- Use ||
- Use ! at least once
- Make decisions using variables rather than hard-coded conditions

Your program should have at least 3 different possible outcomes. For example, a robot might decide whether it is ready to shoot, needs to recharge, or should move somewhere else. Show these decisions by printing what decision the robot made.
You choose the scenario and the variables. Make sure the decisions in your program actually make sense.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 8 - Arrays
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Arrays lesson on Codecademy. Arrays allow you to store multiple values of the same type in one variable. In this assignment, you will practice creating, accessing, and changing values in an array.

Template: Main class with the main method.

Your task:
Create an array containing information related to a topic of your choice. Examples include test scores, game scores, sensor readings, temperatures, or ages.
Your program must:
- Create an array containing at least 5 values
- Print at least 3 individual values from the array using their indexes
- Change at least one value in the array
- Print the changed value
- Print the length of the array using .length

Do not use a loop for this assignment. The goal is to practice working with individual array elements before combining arrays with loops.

assignments.name: Java Lesson 10 - Loops
assignments.description:
Complete after doing the Loops lesson on Codecademy. Loops allow your program to repeat code without writing the same instructions over and over. This assignment is your first larger problem-solving assignment: you will need to decide what your program should do and determine how a loop can accomplish it.

Template: Main class with the main method.

Your task:
Create an array or ArrayList containing a collection of numerical data. Your program should analyze the data and report useful information about it.
Your program must:
- Use at least one loop
- Examine every value in the collection
- Calculate a total or sum
- Find the largest value
- Find the smallest value
- Calculate the average
- Print the results

You may choose what the numbers represent. For example, they could be test scores, match scores, sensor readings, temperatures, or anything else that makes sense.
You should use a loop to process the collection rather than manually working with each value. Basically, pretend you don’t know the size or contents of the array.
